checks.ref:
command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
review="$reports/review-code.md"
added=$(git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- "$review" | tail -1)
base=HEAD
[ -z "$added" ] || base="$added^"
touched=$({ git diff --name-only "$base"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | grep -vxF "$review" | grep -v '^\.gnomish-task/' || true)
[ -z "$touched" ] || { echo "$touched"; echo "the review-code stage writes nothing but $review - restore the files above with: git checkout $base -- <file>"; exit 1; }

findings.message: R3 Fix contradicts design.md D5 and ignores existing precedent: D5 says the committed file is 'compact, one city per line so diffs are reviewable', but the proposed fix runs `biome format --write` on city-data/geonames-cities.json from city-data:compile; the current biome-formatted committed file already splits 109 city tuples over several lines (lines matching `^\s+\[\s*$`), so the fix would lock in a format that breaks D5. packages/client/biome.json already excludes the generated zone-rules data file (`"includes": ["**", "!zone-rules/release.json"]`); excluding city-data/geonames-cities.json the same way keeps serializeCityDataset's one-city-per-line output and adds no dependency. Fix risk mentions neither D5 nor this precedent, and the fix adds an outside process (biome on PATH) and a new failure path to the compile command.

Task 9.2 is marked ✅ without evidence: tasks.md 9.2 requires 'Score ≥ 95% (minimum 90%)' for runs that include src/adapters/city-search/cityTextMatching.ts, createCompositeCitySearch.ts, fetchCitySearch.ts and zoneCitiesSource.ts, and the review's own Mutation section says these and parseGeoNamesCityData.ts 'could not be measured', while compileCityData.ts (90.29%), download.ts (90.91%), selectCityNames.ts (93.55%) and parseGeoNamesRows.ts (95.24%; 1 survived, 1 no coverage) stay below or at the edge of the target with survivors left. The review rates M7 ⚠️ on the same facts, so 9.2 should be ⚠️/❌, not ✅.
